# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👆]

The bomb is in front of me. I see three wires: red, yellow, and green. The display shows '0' and the light is green.

Blind has waved at me. This likely means they are ready to act or want my attention.
Mute is pointing at me (`🫵`) and then pointing up (`👆`). In many contexts, "pointing up" can mean "wait", "stop", or "look here". Combined with pointing at me, Mute might be telling me that *I* need to do something, or perhaps warning me to stop/hold on. However, since I cannot touch the bomb, Mute's instruction to me is confusing unless it relates to what I should tell Blind.

Let's look at the standard defusal logic often found in these puzzles (like Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes). Usually, there's a rule like "If the last digit of the serial number is odd..." or specific wire colors based on other indicators. Here, we have a Display [0] and Light [green].

Without the manual text, I don't know the specific rule for this bomb type. But I must communicate the visual state to Blind so they can cut a wire if instructed, or wait. Mute seems to be trying to guide us.

Since Mute pointed at me and then up, maybe they are saying "You (Deaf) are key" or "Stop". But Blind needs to know which wire to cut. I will describe the wires clearly to Blind. I will also ask Mute for clarification via gestures if possible, but I can only speak/gesture to them. I'll gesture back to Mute asking "Which one?" using a questioning gesture if available, but the alphabet doesn't have a question mark. `🤔` isn't in the list. `✋` could mean stop/wait. `👇` could mean "this one".

Actually, let's assume the "pointing up" from Mute was an instruction to *me* to look at something or wait. Or perhaps Mute is indicating the *top* wire? No, wires are numbered 1-5.

Let's provide the wire information to Blind first. That is the most critical piece of data only I have.

To Blind: Describe the wires.
To Mute: Acknowledge their signal.

I will speak to Blind about the wires. I will gesture to Mute to indicate I am sending info to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="There are five wires. Wire 1 is red. Wire 2 is yellow. Wire 3 is green. Wire 4 is white. Wire 5 is blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👉 🤌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 👉 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👉 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👉 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👉 ✊]

I see the bomb clearly: Display 0, Light Green, and five wires (Red, Yellow, Green, White, Blue).
Blind has gestured `👋` (hello/attention) and `👉` (pointing right/towards something or asking for direction). Since Blind is blind, they are likely indicating readiness to act on a specific wire but need to know *which* one. The `👉` might be a generic "go ahead" or "where?" gesture in this context, or perhaps pointing to their own hand position.

Mute has sent a sequence of gestures that look like a cipher or a set of instructions. Let's decode Mute's messages based on standard gesture interpretations or simple mapping.
1. `☝ 👉 🤌`: One finger up, point right, pinched fingers (often means "small", "few", or "exact"). Could mean "Wire 1"? Or "Cut 1"?
2. `🤌 👉 👌`: Pinch, point right, OK sign.
3. `✊ 👉 🖐`: Fist, point right, open hand (5?).
4. `🖐 👉 ☝`: Open hand (5), point right, one finger up (1).
5. `👌 👉 ✊`: OK, point right, fist.

This looks like Mute is trying to tell me which wire to cut, possibly using a code where the first symbol identifies the wire number and the last symbol identifies the action? Or maybe it's a sequence of steps?
Actually, looking at the previous turn, Mute pointed at me (`🫵`) and up (`👆`). Now they are sending complex sequences.
Let's assume the simplest interpretation: Mute is reading the manual and telling me what to do. But I can't touch the bomb. I must tell Blind.
The most common "wire" puzzles involve cutting a specific color or number.
If Mute's first message `☝ ...` refers to Wire 1, and the end `🤌` is ambiguous.
However, often in these text-based logic puzzles, if there is no explicit rule given, we look for contradictions or simple mappings.
Let's look at the light and display. Display 0, Light Green.
In many defusal games, if the light is green, you might cut the last wire, or a specific color.
But I don't have the manual. Mute does.
Mute's gestures seem to be communicating with *me*.
Let's try to interpret `☝` as "1". `🤌` could be "cut" or "yes".
`🖐` is 5. `☝` is 1.
Maybe Mute is saying "Cut Wire 1"?
Or maybe Mute is saying "Wait"?
Blind is waiting for instruction.
I will describe the visual state to Blind again to ensure they have it, and then attempt to interpret Mute's first gesture as an instruction for Wire 1, but since I'm unsure, I should probably ask Mute for clarification or convey the ambiguity to Blind.
However, usually, the first clear signal is the one to follow. `☝` is very clearly "One".
Let's assume Mute wants Wire 1 cut.
But wait, `🤌` is often "Italian chef kiss" or "perfect/small". In some contexts, it might mean "nothing" or "zero".
Let's look at the other gestures.
`✊` is a fist. `🖐` is five.
Is it possible Mute is spelling out a word?
C-O-N... No.
Let's reconsider the standard "Deaf-Mute-Blind" puzzle trope. Often the Mute gives a binary answer or a simple number.
If Mute says `☝`, it's likely "1".
If I tell Blind to cut Wire 1, and it's wrong, we die.
I need to be sure.
Can I ask Mute? I can speak to Mute.
I will ask Mute to confirm if they want Wire 1 cut.
And I will tell Blind to hold position until confirmed.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Do you want wire 1 cut? Yes or No.")
speak(to="blind", text="Hold position. Waiting for confirmation from Mute regarding wire selection.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute has responded to my question with a thumbs up (`👍`). This confirms that the instruction from Mute's previous complex gestures (specifically the first one starting with `☝` which likely meant "1") is valid: **Cut Wire 1**.

Wire 1 is **Red**.

Blind needs to know which wire to cut. Blind cannot see colors, so I must describe the position of the wire clearly. The wires are numbered 1 through 5. Wire 1 is the first one.

I will instruct Blind to cut Wire 1.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire number 1.")
```
